about: The vendored copies of third-party packages that carry no package.json of their own, inside a package of @requestport/web's notices (Plan 13, H.7 round 7; ruling 199 item 1). scripts/pack-requestport.mjs's listedVendoredPackages reads it: an entry names the installed package that holds the copy (holder, by name, and its version) and the copy's path there, the copy's SHA-256, what was read to review it (reviewed), and the packages it bundles, each with the licence its package.json declares and the text of its licence file, which THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES enters by itself as <name>@<version> (vendored in <holder>@<version>). An entry whose holder the notices cover at another version, or whose file there is missing or at another SHA-256, refuses the pack, so a changed copy is reviewed here before it ships; an entry whose holder the notices do not cover adds nothing. Each bundled text is the licence file of that version's npm tarball (the tarball its entry's from names by its sha512), its trailing white space dropped. An entry for a bundler's runtime, which a holder's own files carry (esbuild's helpers, rolldown's runtime; ruling 210 item 2), names one file of the holder's that carries it, not each, and the bundler at the version packages/core installs, whose licence text it gives: no holder's build records the version of the bundler that wrote it. scripts/pack-requestport.test.mjs holds each entry's file against its holder's as this tree installs it, and each bundled text against a SHA-256 that case pins. A copy with no package.json, no licence comment, no source map and no entry here is what the notices cannot see.

copies.reviewed: H.7 round 7, 2026-10-12, at @trigger.dev/core 4.6.4 (both copies this tree installs, one per zod peer, hold this file byte for byte). It is esbuild's bundle of superjson 2.2.1, which @trigger.dev/core's own scripts/bundle-superjson.mjs writes (its package.json's bundle-vendor script; superjson is a development dependency of it, not a dependency), opening with the comment 'Bundled superjson v2.2.1 … Original package: https://github.com/flightcontrolhq/superjson … License: MIT', which names no copyright holder and is no licence comment as the pack reads one. Its module path comments name node_modules/.pnpm/superjson@2.2.1, is-what@4.1.16 and copy-anything@3.0.5 and no other package. It carries no source map, and no package.json between it and @trigger.dev/core's root names a package (dist/esm/package.json names none). It is the copy the package's ESM build imports (dist/esm/v3/imports/superjson.js), and the one the self-host build compiles in (H.7 round 6's check; H.7 round 7's measuring build at 4a57b4d3). The rest of it is the bundler's module wrapper.

copies.reviewed: J.8, ruling 210's round, 2026-10-14, at drizzle-orm 0.45.2. Ruling 209's round's scan of the self-host build's contained files (track-j.md, 'Item 3', at 333625be's seed) found 106 of its .cjs files binding esbuild's runtime helpers in esbuild's CommonJS form ('"use strict";' then 'var __defProp = Object.defineProperty;' and the rest at the start of a line), eleven names among them: __copyProps, __create, __defProp, __export, __getOwnPropDesc, __getOwnPropNames, __getProtoOf, __hasOwnProp, __reExport, __toCommonJS and __toESM. This file is the first of them, sorted, and binds seven; 442 of the package's 888 JavaScript files bind one, all of them this holder at this version, which the notices enter esbuild for once. Its source map names drizzle-orm's own ../src/alias.ts alone, and it carries no licence comment. The holder's build records no version of the esbuild that wrote it: the entry gives esbuild 0.28.2, the esbuild packages/core installs, and its LICENSE.md, which is byte for byte the LICENSE.md of each esbuild this tree installs (0.18.20, 0.23.1, 0.25.12 and 0.28.2) (ruling 210 item 2).

copies.reviewed: J.8, ruling 210's round, 2026-10-14, at @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.1.0; reviewed again for ruling 236, 2026-10-21, at 2.3.0, whose npm tarball holds this file byte for byte as 2.1.0's does (both tarballs read, and compared; 2.2.0's holds it too), so what follows is true of it at 2.3.0, its CommonJS twin dist/chunk-Bnu9O96Y.cjs is unchanged as well, and 2.3.0's package.json declares tsdown ^0.18.0 as 2.1.0's does. Ruling 209's round's scan of the self-host build's contained files (track-j.md, 'Item 3', at 333625be's seed) found this file binding nine names of esbuild's runtime helpers: __commonJSMin, __copyProps, __create, __defProp, __getOwnPropDesc, __getOwnPropNames, __getProtoOf, __hasOwnProp and __toESM. It is rolldown's runtime, not esbuild's: the file is that runtime alone, between '//#region rolldown:runtime' and '//#endregion', beside rolldown's own __exportAll, from the package's tsdown build (tsdown, a development dependency at ^0.18.0, runs rolldown). It carries no source map and no licence comment. Rolldown is entered for it, as ruling 210 item 2 has it, and esbuild is not. The holder's build records no version of the rolldown that wrote it: the entry gives rolldown 1.2.4, the rolldown packages/core installs, and its LICENSE, whose last line points to rolldown's THIRD-PARTY-LICENSE, the licences of the works parts of rolldown derive from (rollup's and esbuild's MIT texts, in the copy installed beside it) (ruling 210 item 2).
